'''Jrue Randall Holiday''' (born June 12, 1990 in [[Chatsworth, California]]) is an [[United States|American]] former [[college basketball]] player for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]]. His older brother Justin plays for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]].

==High school==
Holiday attended [[Campbell Hall School]] and was ranked as one of the best college recruits in the nation in the class of 2008. He was ranked #2 in the nation by [[Rivals.com]] and #4 by Scout.com.<ref>[http://scouthoops.scout.com/a.z?s=75&p=9&c=4&pid=88&yr=2008 Scout.com Class of 2008 Basketball Rankings]</ref>

He played on the varsity basketball team all four years of high school. As a senior he was named the 2008 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]]. In his senior year he averaged 25.9 ppg, 11.2 rpg, 6.9 apg and 4.8 spg and lead Campbell Hall to a 31-5 record and the California Division IV state title.<ref>[http://uclabruins.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/holiday_jrue00.html High School Stats]</ref> Holiday was as a 2008 [[McDonald's All-American Team|McDonald's All-American]] where he scored 14 points and had five rebounds, five steals and three assists for the West Team. He also participated in the 2008 [[Jordan Brand]] Classic.

==College==
In July 2007, Holiday committed to play basketball at [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. He chose UCLA over [[University of Washington|Washington]]. 

Holiday had 11 points in his first career regular season game in a December 4, 2008 win over [[Prairie View A&M]].<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283170026 Collison, freshmen keep No. 4 UCLA on track as Bruins humble Prairie View]</ref>

On April 9, 2009, after one season playing at UCLA, Holiday said he plans to make himself eligible for the [[NBA draft]]. He also said that he will not hire an agent as to maintain his NCAA eligibility.<ref>[http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2009/news/story?id=4056438 Holiday to enter NBA draft]</ref>
